1:72 to 75mm: Small Scale Up to Full Display

A massive 308.6% upscale that turns a tiny 1:72 model into a full display-size piece with broad, paintable surfaces.

The math

(75.0mm / 24.3mm) × 100 = 308.6%

Based on 175cm human baseline, eye-level measurement (160cm).

Scale baselines

  • Source eye level22.2mm Eye
  • Target eye level75.0mm Eye
  • Scale factor308.6%

The extreme upscale

Tripling and change a 1:72 kit into 75mm display territory is a research/display move. The smooth, simplified surfaces are ideal for practice painting or finishing experiments on a recognizable subject.

Commit to the build

3.09x is the largest jump in the matrix. This is a dedicated multi-part, multi-plate project. I break it into sections, print at a fine profile, and accept the time and material cost for a substantial display shelf piece.

How I got this number

By kitsorix, 3D printing hobbyist

This percentage comes from a 175cm human baseline with eye-level at 160cm. I print the result on my Bambu Lab A1 Mini and measure with digital calipers before I post it.

I test every percentage on FDM before publishing. PLA and PETG cool with minimal dimensional change — typically under 0.5%. If a number fails on my machine, I adjust it.

Full methodology →

Quick Answers

Is 308.6% too much to print?

It is the biggest jump, but for a display piece it works — just plan a multi-part build and expect long, material-heavy printing.
